# FDG7033

> DO NOT handle non-CLS-compliant exceptions (exceptions that don’t derive from `System.Exception`) using a parameterless catch block.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 7.2.2 Exception Handling.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1031
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: draft

CA1031 reports a parameterless catch whose block does not throw, which handles every exception, non-CLS-compliant ones included. Its reports of catches of System.Exception and System.SystemException belong to FDG7025, FDG7026, FDG7038 and FDG7039. Since CLR 2.0 a catch of System.Exception also receives non-CLS-compliant exceptions wrapped in RuntimeWrappedException, as the body says. CA1031 has no code fix.

## From the book

Languages that support non-`Exception`-derived exceptions are free to handle these exceptions.

```csharp
try{ ... }
catch{ ... }
```

CLR 2.0 has been modified to deliver noncompliant exceptions to compliant catch blocks wrapped up in `RuntimeWrappedException`.
